sources: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models (OpenAI Codex models and plans, read 2026-11-11)
skills/dual-model-review/SKILL.md as of 2026-10 (vendor system cards, API price lists, third-party effort sweeps; not re-checked on 2026-11-11)

models.gpt-6-astra: Most capable model for complex work across code, apps, and research. The flagship; one env var away (CODEX_MODEL).
models.gpt-6.1-sol: Near-Astra performance at a lower cost, for repeated, long-running work. Efforts: low, medium, high, xhigh. The default for both skills.
models.gpt-6.1-terra: Clear writing, visual understanding and computer use. Needs Codex CLI 0.159.0 or later. Considered and not chosen: newer than Sol, but not aimed at code review or argument.

notes.text: OpenAI: on Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu plans, choose GPT-6.1 Sol (gpt-6.1-sol) when available. GPT-6.1 Terra reached Codex on those plans on 2026-10-26. gpt-5.5 was retired from Codex with ChatGPT sign-in on 2026-10-14; the 5.4 line and older are retired too. Debate's previous default, the 5.6 Sol id, is no longer listed, which is why debate moved to the same default as review.

Both subscription arms of dual-model-review fit a $20 plan: Claude Opus 5.5 is inside Claude Pro's limits (Claude Fable 5.1 is not; it bills as usage credits there), and GPT-6.1 Sol is included for ChatGPT Plus in Codex.
notes.source: vendor plan pages, carried over from SKILL.md

notes.text: The Claude Opus 5.5 system card's FrontierCode Main score is 54.6% at medium and 54.4% at max: flat. The Claude Opus 5 card explains the shape: at higher effort the model makes more changes than the task asks for. One effort sweep on a code-review benchmark (CodeRabbit, Claude Opus 5) found xhigh more precise but lower recall.
notes.source: Anthropic system cards, CodeRabbit sweep, carried over from SKILL.md

notes.text: GLM-5.2 via Zen stalled repeatedly: one low-effort run on a 591-byte packet ran 44 minutes and never returned; one max-effort run on a 75KB packet returned empty after about 10 minutes. Kimi K3 returned in under three minutes on the same packet. Two observations, not a benchmark.
